status_summary: Public Law 119-21, approved 2025-07-04, added Medicaid provisions that align with parts of this recommendation: address verification from 2027-01-01 and a federal duplicate-enrollment check from 2029-10-01 (section 71103), quarterly death file checks for enrollees from 2027-01-01 and for providers from 2028-01-01 (sections 71104 and 71105), a requirement from fiscal year 2030 that the Secretary issue eligibility-related disallowances for state error rates above 3 percent, with the Secretary's good-faith waiver authority restricted (section 71106), six-month redeterminations for the expansion adult group from 2027-01-01 (section 71107) and a $1 million home equity cap for long-term care eligibility from 2028-01-01 (section 71108). These are enacted and have drawn CMS guidance (an informational bulletin of 2025-11-18 and a State Medicaid Director Letter of 2026-03-06), but none is operative before 2027-01-01. No enhanced contingency fee, expanded 90/10 match for fraud systems or waiver-free positive-return programs was found, and the managed care provisions found are limited to a duty for plans to send address data to states (section 71103) and a bar on plans determining community engagement compliance (section 71119).

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 was approved. Its Medicaid chapter includes sections 71103 (duplicate enrollment and address verification), 71104 and 71105 (deceased enrollees and providers), 71106 (payment reduction for certain erroneous excess payments), 71107 (eligibility redeterminations) and 71108 (home equity limit).
CMS issues State Medicaid Director Letter #26-001 on six-month eligibility renewals for the adult expansion group (section 71107), for renewals on or after 2027-01-01.

title: Medicaid program integrity: contingency fees, improper eligibility penalties, asset tests
uncertainties: Mandate text on page 467 was checked. Sections 71103 to 71106 were read in the CMS informational bulletin of 2025-11-18 and sections 71103 to 71108 in the CMS legislation overview slide on the medicaid.gov host; section 71107 was read in State Medicaid Director Letter #26-001. The GovInfo body text of Public Law 119-21 is truncated before Subtitle B, so the statutory text, including the $1 million home equity amount (taken from the MACPAC September 2025 summary), was not read. The CMS bulletin states that the 3 percent error-rate threshold existed in prior law and that section 71106 restricts rather than removes the Secretary's waiver authority. No enhanced contingency fee or 90/10 match for fraud systems appears in the CMS summaries; this is an absence in summaries, not a check of the statute. Federal Register queries for implementing rules on these sections were not run. Work requirements and cost sharing are covered in c14-05, whose proposal also includes more robust eligibility determinations, so this record overlaps c14-05 on that one item.
